title: Neapeague (Napeague Beach)
summary: Neapeague, now commonly Napeague, is the sandy and marshy water-land connecting Montauk with the main part of Long Island in East Hampton town.
map_geometry_source: approximate modern Napeague Beach marker; not exact historical boundary or whale-rights coordinate
introduction_title: The Water-Land Between Amagansett And Montauk
introduction_content: Neapeague is connected with the long sandy and marshy beach between the Amagansett hills and Montauk. The placename remains visible in modern Napeague, Napeague Beach, and Napeague Bay.
history_content: Neapeague is part of the Montaukett eastern Long Island landscape, where beach, marsh, whale, and fish contexts are closely connected. Dated source context appear in the Historic Timeline.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Neapeague, Napeake, Napeage, Napeag, Napeague, Nap-peag, Nap-peeg, and Niepeage. The name is interpreted as water land, from Montauk dialect elements for water and land.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are therefore important symbolic markers in preserving or changing cultural identities, and in marking or facilitating socio-political changes and relations.”

— Herman Beyer, Matthias Brenzinger, Theodorus du Plessis, and Peter E. Raper, editors, Critical Toponymy: Place Names in Political, Historical and Commercial Landscape (2019), Publisher description

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is an approximate general point for Napeague Beach, the narrow sandy stretch between Amagansett and Montauk, not an exact boundary for older beach, marsh, or whale-rights descriptions.
